keyFindings.text: **P1 — Branch isolation is documented with an unsupported or underspecified merge implication.** Official documentation confirms creating, inspecting, and deleting page branches for isolated work. The local reference says edits remain isolated “until the branch merges” and calls branching a staging pattern, but the cited page action inventory contains create/delete/details/list operations and no merge action or merge procedure. Qualify the claim to the supported lifecycle and explicitly document whether merge is outside this MCP surface. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:133-137] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:296-312]

**P1 — Breakpoint behavior is represented as read-only and indirect, while the official boundary includes changing the current breakpoint.** The packet documents `get_all_breakpoints` as a canvas-bound read and says responsive behavior flows indirectly through styles, but it does not state whether changing the active/current breakpoint is supported by the exposed remote version or is only a Designer UI operation. Official documentation explicitly includes reading or changing current breakpoints among the Bridge-App-dependent capabilities and separately promises responsive layouts across breakpoints. Reconcile the action inventory with the hosted capability claim, then add a version-qualified breakpoint-selection/verification scenario. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:123-129] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/design/designer.md:71-82] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:443-469]

**P1 — Canvas navigation/state is classified inconsistently.** The packet correctly says that canvas-bound page, mode, branch, component-view, selection, navigation, snapshots, and breakpoint operations need the Bridge App, and that data-plane operations can work without the canvas. However, `designer-capabilities.md` says that only `create_page_folder` and `open_canvas` are draft-write actions in this group, while the packet's own action table marks `close_component_view`, `open_component_view`, `select_element`, and `switch_page` as `DW`. The official documentation and repository README confirm the Bridge App/live-canvas boundary, but do not turn canvas navigation into site-tree content writes. The packet should distinguish Bridge-bound state/navigation mutations from site-tree draft writes and align the gate/class labels. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: https://github.com/webflow/mcp-server] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:25-48] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:443-469]

**P1 — Element-tree discovery is too concise for reliable targeting.** Official Webflow documentation says elements can be found by type, text, style, tag, attribute, or component. The local packet names `query_elements` and `get_all_elements` but gives no query-key schema or worked selector examples; the action reference exposes only an opaque `queries[]` parameter. Add the supported query dimensions, target-id shape, and one discovery-to-mutation example to the shared Designer reference and payload/manual coverage. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:52-60] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:188-207]

**P1 — Style coverage omits official class/combo-class and raw-CSS semantics.** The official surface describes reusing or creating classes and combo classes, editing CSS properties, building styles from raw CSS, and managing styles across breakpoints. The local reference instead describes named styles, `properties[]`, and variable-mode bindings, without explaining class/combo-class identity or raw-CSS input. Add those distinctions and a safe create/update/read-back example; otherwise a reader can mistake the named-style lifecycle for the complete Designer style model. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:86-95] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:374-389]

**P1 — The component-variants feature card is stale and contradicts the packet's authoritative action table.** Official documentation promises full component support for props, variants, slots, and metadata. The variant card claims “eight” actions but invents/assumes `update_variant`, `set_default_variant`, and generic list/get actions, while omitting the action-reference entries `duplicate_variant`, `set_variant_name`, `reorder_variants`, `set_variant_styles`, and `get_variant_styles`. Rewrite the card from the action table, including exact parameters and risk classes, and add a deterministic variant read/update/read-back scenario. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/design/component-variants.md:11-41] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:173-184]

**P2 — Component metadata, prop constraints, and slot behavior are listed but not operationally specified.** The shared reference gives useful high-level semantics for props, slots, variants, and component-view scoping, and it lists `set_component_metadata`, but it does not show metadata fields, prop type/default rules, slot validation, or a metadata/prop/slot read-back contract. This is concision/completeness debt rather than a missing safety boundary; add a component-builder example and verification checklist to the Designer card or payload/manual assets. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:98-119] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/design/designer.md:71-82] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:137-184]

**P2 — Variable-mode coverage is a useful workflow summary but lacks mode/value/read-back detail.** The packet correctly describes collections, modes, typed variables, style bindings, and a second theme mode. It does not explain how per-mode values are populated and verified, how multiple bindings are inspected/removed, or whether the active canvas mode can be changed through the exposed action surface. Official documentation frames variables as design-system primitives for color schemes, typography, and spacing; expand the local mode matrix without claiming an unexposed active-mode operation. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:86-95] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:374-417]

**P0 — Contradictory CMS publish-target semantics.** The remote action inventory and Data API publish endpoint define `publish_collection_items` with a collection and item IDs, not a domain or staging flag; the local baseline describes it as deploying drafts to live, and the CMS card explicitly says CMS item publish has no staging-domain target. However, the publish/deploy card labels the same action “staging-first” and its prompt says to publish collection drafts to the staging subdomain. That contradiction can make an operator believe an item publish is isolated to `*.webflow.io` when the item endpoint itself has no domain selector. Reconcile the card and prompts: describe item publish as a separate live CMS publish, reserve staging-subdomain language for `publish_site`, and add a confirmation/refusal scenario that prevents domain assumptions. [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:100-119] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/tool-surface.md:67-73] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/content/cms.md:26-35] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/content/publish-deploy.md:20-35] [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/reference/cms/collection-items/staged-items/publish-item.md] [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/docs/ai-tools.md]

**P0 — Missing/unsafe CMS draft encoding.** The local payload example labels a request “CREATE A DRAFT COLLECTION ITEM” but sends only `fieldData`; the CMS pairing scenario likewise calls `create_collection_items` “(draft)” without an explicit draft field. Official Data API schemas expose `isDraft`, `isArchived`, `lastPublished`, and `cmsLocaleId`, while the official MCP guidance says items may be created directly in the live site or as queued/drafted items. The official OSS adapter accepts `isDraft` and defaults an omitted value to `false`, so the packet's example is not a reliable draft contract on the local surface. Add an explicit `isDraft: true` example, state remote/local differences beside the payload, and require a read-back assertion of `isDraft`, `lastPublished`, and locale before treating the write as draft-safe. [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/assets/payload-examples.md:48-55] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/manual-testing-playbook/pairing/pair-data.md:24-46] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/content/cms.md:22-37] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/SKILL.md:167-170] [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/docs/ai-tools.md] [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/reference/cms/collection-items/staged-items/create-item.md] [SOURCE: https://github.com/webflow/mcp-server/blob/main/src/tools/cms.ts]

**P1 — Missing publish completion and staged-blast-radius checks.** The official site-publish contract returns `202 Accepted`, requires either `customDomains` or `publishToWebflowSubdomain`, accepts an optional `pageId`, limits successful publish queues to one per minute, and warns that promoting staging to production publishes all staged changes after multiple page-to-staging publishes. The local feature card records the queue and broad staging rule, but the staging example and SAFE-001 scenario only capture a receipt and staged URL; they do not distinguish accepted from completed, assert `publishScope`, or test the “all staged changes” promotion case. Add a staging single-page scenario plus a separately gated production-promotion scenario with explicit domain choice, page/site scope, receipt fields, and post-publish verification. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/reference/sites/publish.md] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/content/publish-deploy.md:20-37] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/assets/examples/staging-publish.md:31-40] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/manual-testing-playbook/safety-gate/pubgate.md:20-30] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/assets/payload-examples.md:84-94]

**P1 — Missing remote/local page-branch lifecycle contract.** Official MCP documentation describes creating, inspecting, and deleting page branches. The remote action reference exposes `create_branch`, `list_branches`, `get_branch_details`, and `delete_branch`, but the local site-pages card says “page branches (create/update)” even though no `update_branch` action is listed, and the Designer reference says isolation lasts “until the branch merges” without identifying a merge action. The official OSS `dePages.ts` source exposes page creation/folders/current-page/switch-page but no branch lifecycle, so this is also a surface-boundary gap. Add a remote-only branch matrix with parent-page/current-branch readbacks, create/list/details/delete coverage, an explicit “merge is not exposed here” statement, and a deletion confirmation scenario; do not imply an automatic merge. This refines the prior merge concern with new surface-split and manual-coverage evidence. [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp] [SOURCE: https://github.com/webflow/mcp-server/blob/main/src/tools/dePages.ts] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:296-312] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/action-reference.md:443-463] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/feature-catalog/content/site-pages-scripts.md:21-31] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/references/designer-capabilities.md:133-148] [SOURCE: .opencode/specs/mcp-tooling/015-mcp-webflow/011-deep-research-quality-gaps/research/lineages/luna-max-fast/iterations/iteration-001.md:15]

**P1 — Too concise CMS read verification.** The read-only example and READ-001 scenario stop after “collection items returned,” and the draft pairing scenario stops after the create call. They do not require recording whether the returned item is draft or live, whether it is archived, which locale was addressed, or whether `lastPublished` changed. Those fields are part of the official item model, and the publish API also supports locale-specific item publication. Add before/after assertions and a locale-aware readback step to the CMS read and draft scenarios; otherwise a successful read cannot prove which content state the workflow inspected. [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/assets/examples/read-cms-content.md:31-41] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/manual-testing-playbook/read-only/readcms.md:20-30] [SOURCE: .opencode/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-webflow/manual-testing-playbook/pairing/pair-data.md:20-30] [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/reference/cms/collection-items/staged-items/create-item.md] [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/reference/cms/collection-items/staged-items/update-item.md] [SOURCE: https://developers.webflow.com/data/reference/cms/collection-items/staged-items/publish-item.md]

**P1 — Too concise page-settings publish boundary.** The official repository's pages tool describes page metadata reads as returning draft/published status and page-settings updates as including publishing status. The local packet acknowledges that `update_page_settings` can flip status, but the draft payload/example and DRAFT-001 scenario show no concrete body, status omission rule, or postcondition that the status stayed unchanged. The official changelog also records that slug updates can be silently ignored for home, collection-template, utility, and some secondary-locale pages. Add a status-safe DW payload, a separate explicit PB payload, and read-back checks for status and returned fields; document the slug/page-type/locale caveat so a `200` is not treated as proof that every requested setting applied. **P2 — Missing item-publish/unpublish payload and manual coverage.** The remote action inventory includes both `publish_collection_items` and `unpublish_collection_items`, and the official publish schema supports bulk primary-locale IDs and locale-specific `cmsLocaleIds` with a response containing published IDs and errors. The packet has a CMS card row for publish/unpublish but its payload asset contains only draft creation and site publishing, while the manual playbook covers CMS reads and site publishing rather than item publish/unpublish. Add primary- and secondary-locale payload shapes, confirmation expectations, partial-error handling, and a deterministic publish-then-unpublish scenario. **P0 — Custom-code release and gate semantics conflict across the packet’s remote/local documentation.** The remote action reference classifies registration, application, freeform-code, and script-set actions as draft writes, while `mcp-wiring.md` groups “script registration” with deploy actions that require confirmation; the operations card also says scripts “ship with publish.” The local OSS baseline exposes only a smaller seven-action scripts module. Official OSS code shows that inline-site-script handling registers a script and then applies it, that inline scripts are limited to 2,000 characters, and that page upsert replaces all existing page scripts. The packet therefore lacks one surface-specific contract for whether registration/application is draft-write, publish-adjacent, or deploy-gated. This is a P0 boundary gap because an agent could select a weaker gate or report custom code as live without a clear release rule. Reconcile `references/mcp-wiring.md`, `references/tool-surface.md`, `feature-catalog/operations/sitemap-scripts-assets-whtml.md`, and `feature-catalog/content/site-pages-scripts.md`; add a remote-vs-OSS matrix, replacement/length semantics, and a confirmation plus read-back scenario for custom-code changes. **P1 — Asset and image-compression coverage lacks the task lifecycle, payload, read-back, and remote/local boundary.** Official MCP documentation promises asset/folder list, organization, update, deletion, and compression jobs. The remote action reference provides `compress_assets(site_id, asset_ids[], format)`, task list/get actions, upload-by-URL, preview, folder operations, and asset metadata operations; the local operations card reduces this to “upload/update assets” and “compression requests.” The payload asset has no asset example and the 17-scenario playbook has no asset/compression scenario. Official Data API asset responses include `localeId` and `folderId` filtering plus size, alt text, responsive variants, quality, and variant errors. The official OSS `deAsset.ts` source only covers Designer folders/assets/update and image preview, while the local baseline has no data-assets/compression module. Add a remote-vs-OSS matrix, asset/compression payloads, task polling and variant read-back, and an isolated deletion/compression scenario that distinguishes `data_assets_tool` from Designer `asset_tool`. **P1 — Broader page/site metadata coverage omits the schema-markup and structured-data action family.** Official MCP documentation says page management includes schema markup and structured data in addition to SEO metadata and Open Graph tags. The remote action reference exposes `bulk_update_pages_schema_markup` and `query_pages_schema_markup`, but the local site/pages card only names page listing, metadata reads, and SEO/OG/slug/title settings. Add the missing schema/query actions, request fields, site/page/locale applicability, bulk-selection gate, and read-back assertions to `feature-catalog/content/site-pages-scripts.md`, the shared references, and a dedicated manual scenario. This finding is limited to schema/structured-data and metadata coverage; it does not repeat iteration 2’s page status/slug boundary. **P1 — Forms and submissions are listed without a schema, scope, mutation, or evidence contract.** The remote action table has seven distinct form actions, including form-schema reads, per-form and site-wide submission reads, submission update, and destructive deletion; the local feature card only summarizes “related reads” and deletion. None of the 17 manual scenarios is a form scenario, and the payload asset contains no form or submission shape. Official Data API evidence shows that form reads include field definitions, response settings, page/form identifiers, and pagination; submission reads require both `site_id` and `form_id` and return submission date, arbitrary `formResponse`, `localeId`, and pagination. Add an exact action table and payload example to `feature-catalog/content/localization-fonts-forms.md` and `assets/payload-examples.md`, plus a manual scenario covering per-form versus site scope, pagination, locale, update read-back, redacted response evidence, and confirmation before deletion. **P1 — The localization card advertises locale management and deletion that the exposed action surface does not provide.** The card calls the capability “localization (locales + secondary-locale content),” lists generic localization deletes as destructive, and gives “list the locales” and “add a Spanish locale” examples. The remote action reference instead exposes only content/component reads and updates plus static-content updates, all with an explicit `localeId`; it has no locale-create, locale-list, or localization-delete action. Official MCP limitations also state that new localized CMS items cannot be created and that existing CMS/static content is read or updated in secondary locales. The official repository’s tool directory and local OSS baseline do not expose a localization module. Rewrite the card as secondary-locale content support, remove unsupported locale-management/delete examples, label remote-only actions, and add a locale-aware read/update/read-back scenario. **P0 — Enterprise robots replacement/deletion lacks a high-impact safety boundary.** The local action table classifies `replace_robots_txt` as an ungated DW action and `delete_robots_txt` as DS, but gives both only `site_id`; the generic DW matrix therefore does not require confirmation before a whole robots policy can be replaced. The local Enterprise card merely says “redirects/robots/well-known create-update / delete.” Official Data API semantics distinguish PATCH (partial update), PUT (complete replacement), and DELETE (remove selected user-agent rules; deleting an empty rule set can make that user-agent unrestricted), all Enterprise-only and scope-gated. The official OSS adapter accepts rule/sitemap bodies for deletion and implements its delete helper through a PATCH-shaped call, demonstrating a surface/version discrepancy that must not be silently collapsed.
